title: Trump calls on Nvidia's board to rehire Jensen Huang despite widening China spy probe
subtitle: A Sunday-night Truth Social post asks the directors to reverse themselves while the FBI, SEC and Senate investigations into the Megaspeed chip-diversion case are still open.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: President Trump posted on Truth Social late Sunday that 'I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang,' and repeated the call to Fox News on Monday. Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 11 after reports surfaced of an affair with a woman tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed, the company at the center of the alleged diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese buyers. Interim CEO Colette Kress has run the company since. Nvidia's board — which last week publicly stated it had no plans to reinstate Huang — has not changed its position. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters the choice should wait on the outcome of the federal investigations.

A sitting president publicly pressuring a public company's board to reinstate a CEO while that CEO is under active federal investigation is extraordinary. It is also narrow: Trump's post is not a directive, and the board's fiduciary duty runs to shareholders, not the White House. But the backdrop matters. Shares fell roughly 14% on Friday on top of the week's SEC accounting probe news, Moody's cut its outlook, and the FBI and Congress are examining whether Nvidia chips were funneled to China via Megaspeed. A return would require the independent investigation launched November 8 to clear Huang personally — a timeline nobody has signaled.

This lands on a company already in crisis mode. Interim CEO Kress said on Tuesday's earnings call the company would be 'far more selective' about AI financing deals; the SEC is examining accounting practices; a House Foreign Affairs Committee disclosure last week showed Commerce approved roughly 580,000 Nvidia chips for China under a revenue-share arrangement, with some approved buyers on the Pentagon's military-ties list. Trump's call lands into the middle of that, and reads less as a personnel suggestion than as a loyalty test aimed at the board. The directors have to weigh governance norms against political pressure in public.

A note for learners: boards exist precisely to make this kind of call independent of political signal. The textbook response is to let the investigation run, let the facts decide, and publish the reasoning. When a reinstatement debate is conducted on social media rather than in the boardroom, watch what the independent directors say in their next 8-K, not what the president posts. The quality of a corporate governance system shows up under exactly this kind of asymmetric pressure.
